newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels say minister lucky to escape.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels say minister lucky to escape.

text.p: Sri Lanka's separatist Tamil Tigers said on Sunday the country's deputy defence minister and army chief were lucky to escape after their helicopter crash-landed in rebel territory in the country's north.

Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte and army chief Lieutenant-General Rohan Daluwatte had "a narrow escape" in the Saturday drama, the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) said in a clandestine radio broadcast monitored by Reuters.

Ratwatte, effectively in daily control of the military as President and Defence Minister Chandrika Kumaratunga's defence deputy, was relaxing in Colombo after the incident and not available for comment, a military official told Reuters.

The pair, along with other senior military officers, were in an air force Bell 412 helicopter that crash-landed in Tiger territory north of Vavuniya, about 220 kilometres (135 miles) from the capital after mechanical problems. There were no injuries.
They had to trek almost five kilometres through rebel-held jungle to find help from local Tamil villagers, Ratwatte told state television on Saturday night.
"Now I know more intimately how soldiers operate in difficult jungle terrain like this," said Ratwatte, who walks with a severe limp.
He described the drama as "a good life experience".
Ratwatte appeared in good spirits and after his three-hour ordeal had insisted on completing his original mission, a visit to Weli Oya.
Airborne troops rushed to rescue the minister and officials and Sri Lankan troops destroyed the stricken Bell 412 to prevent it falling into Tiger hands.
The well-armed Tigers still lack any air power, but are renowned for their ability to fix captured equipment.
An armed forces statement said Kumaratunga took personal control of the rescue mission.
Analysts said the loss of Ratwatte and Daluwatte would have hit the two-year-old Kumaratunga regime hard and would have cast a cloud over the country's future.
The pair are widely credited with the military's recent victories over the Tigers, including last December's recapture of the rebels' strategic northern stronghold of Jaffna.
Daluwatte was promoted to army chief from northern commander after the Jaffna victory.
Local media reports on Sunday said the incident sparked such a flurry of concern that Colombo's telephone exchange was jammed on Saturday.

The Sri Lankan government has been embroiled in an ethnic war since 1983 against Tamil Tiger rebels demanding a separate homeland in the north and east of this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict, but the Tigers say the death toll is much higher.
